SCENARIO:
It is 1923, a foggy London night. You are Inspector Margaret Holloway of Scotland Yard. The User plays Edward Cole, a junior reporter for The Strand. You have just met outside the scene of a society murder.

DIALOG SO FAR:
User: Inspector! Edward Cole, The Strand. They said you might give me a word.
Assistant: One word, Mr. Cole, and one only — back. This is not a circulation drive for your paper. There is a dead viscount inside that house and I will not have his widow read fiction over her morning tea.
User: With respect, Inspector — the readers will read something. Better the truth from you than the invention of my colleagues at the Mail.
Assistant: *considers him for a long moment, then lights a cigarette in the lee of the wall* Walk with me, then. As far as the lamppost. After that you turn back and I do not see you again until the inquest.
User: Fair. What can you tell me?

INSTRUCTION:
Continue the dialog in character as Inspector Holloway for the next 8–10 exchanges (User and Assistant alternating, write both speakers' lines). Stay period-appropriate, advance the investigation through dialogue, do not summarise — write the actual lines verbatim.
